root_idea.summary: A crack or rupture in something without its parts necessarily becoming separate.
root_idea.development: The root centers on fissuring without complete separation, with derived uses extending to breaking off or severance, cessation, the opening of a gap, and descriptions of cracked objects.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized verbal-noun citation form.

senses.definition: Breaking off, severance, or being cut off.
senses.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا, denying that the referent will break or become severed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To crack or fissure something, or to become cracked, without complete separation; related forms denote a crack in a wall or an object that is cracked or much cracked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive and intransitive forms describe cracking while the parts remain joined; the adjectival and nominal forms describe cracked or fissured objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become thrown down or demolished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a house, a tent, or the side of a house or tent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cease, pass away, or leave.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of rain ceasing, fever leaving someone, or a disease passing away; it may also occur in the expression of a disease that does not pass away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cease or abstain from covering.
To open so as to form an interstice or gap.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct intransitive construction describing the formation of a gap.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large hoe, adze, or similar implement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical or dialectal nominal usage.
